records.name: Tokyo Tower
records.description: A 333-meter lattice communications and observation tower in Shiba-koen, completed in 1958 and inspired by the Eiffel Tower. It has two observation decks and a five-story base building called FootTown.

records.name: Zojo-ji Temple
records.description: A Jodo-shu Buddhist temple founded in 1393 that served as the Tokugawa clan's family temple, with six shoguns buried on its grounds. Its 1622 Sangedatsumon gate is the oldest wooden structure in Tokyo; most other buildings were rebuilt after World War II.

tips.text: The temple grounds are free to enter; the on-site Treasure Gallery museum charges a separate admission fee.

records.name: Shiba Park
records.description: A public park of roughly 30 acres established in 1873, centered around Zojo-ji temple. It offers views of Tokyo Tower and contains the Shiba Toshogu shrine and a historic ginkgo tree.

records.name: Sengaku-ji Temple
records.description: A Soto Zen Buddhist temple founded in 1612 by Tokugawa Ieyasu, famous as the burial site of the 47 ronin who avenged their master Asano Naganori in 1702. Their graves were designated a National Historic Site in 1922, and the temple maintains a museum of their belongings.
records.station: Sengakuji Station (Toei Asakusa Line, exit A2)

records.name: Atago Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine established in 1603 under shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu, sitting atop Atagoyama, the highest natural point in Tokyo's 23 wards at 26 meters. It is dedicated to the fire god Homusubi no Mikoto and is known for its steep stone stairway, said to bring success.

records.name: Roppongi Hills
records.description: A large mixed-use development completed in 2003, anchored by the 54-story Mori Tower. It includes the Tokyo City View observation deck on floors 52-54 and Mori Garden, a landscaped Japanese garden with a pond, on the lower grounds.

tips.text: Tokyo City View observation deck is open daily 10:00-22:00 with last admission at 21:30; hours can extend later on weekends.

records.station: Roppongi Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Toei Oedo Line)

records.name: Mori Art Museum
records.description: A contemporary art museum on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower, founded in 2003 by developer Minoru Mori. It hosts large international exhibitions and a permanent collection of roughly 460 works emphasizing Japanese and East Asian contemporary art, and has shown artists including Yayoi Kusama and Ai Weiwei.

tips.text: The museum keeps late hours (until 22:00 most days, 17:00 on Tuesdays); evening visits after 5pm made up about 30% of 2018 attendance.

records.hours: 10:00–22:00 daily except Tuesdays (10:00–17:00 Tuesdays); last admission 30 min before close
records.station: Roppongi Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Toei Oedo Line)
records.address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower 53F, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo

records.name: 21_21 Design Sight
records.description: A design museum in Roppongi that opened in March 2007, created by architect Tadao Ando and fashion designer Issey Miyake. The 1,700-square-meter facility has a split-level concrete structure with a distinctive hand-sanded steel roof and two galleries hosting design-focused exhibitions.

records.name: The National Art Center, Tokyo
records.description: An art center that opened in January 2007 with no permanent collection, instead hosting rotating exhibitions. Designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa with a distinctive wave-like glass facade, it draws over 2.2 million visitors annually, ranking among the world's most-visited art venues.
records.station: Nogizaka Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, exit 6, directly connected); Roppongi Station (4-5 minute walk)

records.name: Suntory Museum of Art
records.description: An art museum on the 3rd floor of Tokyo Midtown Galleria, holding a collection of traditional Japanese art including paintings, ceramics, lacquerware, and glassware, with rotating thematic exhibitions.
records.address: Tokyo Midtown Galleria 3F, 9-7-4 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-8643

records.name: Tokyo Midtown
records.description: A mixed-use development completed in March 2007 across six buildings, centered on Midtown Tower, once the second-tallest building in Tokyo. The complex houses the Suntory Museum of Art and 21_21 Design Sight, and is bordered by Hinokicho Park, a 10-acre public green space.

records.name: Azabudai Hills
records.description: A complex of three skyscrapers in the Azabudai business district that opened in October 2023. Its main tower, Mori JP Tower, stands 325.2 meters tall and became the tallest building in Japan on completion. The 8.1-hectare development combines offices, residences, retail, and extensive green space.
records.station: Kamiyacho Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, directly connected)

records.name: teamLab Borderless
records.description: A digital art museum run by the art collective teamLab, located in the basement of Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B. It presents immersive, borderless digital installations across connected exhibition spaces.

tips.text: Tickets are date- and time-specific and must be booked in advance; admission is roughly ¥3,600-5,600 for ages 18 and up.

records.address: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B, B1F, Toranomon, Minato-ku, Tokyo

records.name: Rainbow Bridge
records.description: A suspension bridge across Tokyo Bay linking Shibaura Pier to the Odaiba waterfront, opened in 1993. Its double-deck design carries the Shuto Expressway above and the Yurikamome transit line, a road, and walkways below. The white towers are illuminated nightly using solar power.
records.address: Minato, Tokyo, Japan (Shibaura Pier to Odaiba)

records.name: Odaiba Marine Park
records.description: A waterfront park on the Odaiba shoreline that hosted the triathlon and marathon swimming events at the 2020 Summer Olympics. It offers a sandy beach view of Tokyo Bay, Rainbow Bridge, and the Statue of Liberty replica.

records.name: Fuji Television Building
records.description: The headquarters of Fuji Television, designed by architect Kenzo Tange and relocated to Odaiba in the late 1990s. The distinctive building, with its large exposed sphere, has become a recognizable part of the Odaiba skyline and helped establish the area as a commercial hub.
records.station: Daiba Station (Yurikamome Line, south exit, 3-minute walk)

records.name: Statue of Liberty Replica (Odaiba)
records.description: A 12.25-meter replica of the Statue of Liberty on the Odaiba waterfront, unveiled in 2000 as a symbol of Japan-France friendship after an earlier temporary loan of the original French statue in 1998-99. It is a popular photo spot with Rainbow Bridge in the background.

tips.text: Free to visit and accessible 24 hours a day.

records.station: Odaiba-kaihinkoen Station or Daiba Station (Yurikamome Line, 3-minute walk)

records.name: Institute for Nature Study
records.description: A nature preserve affiliated with the National Museum of Nature and Science, spanning about 5,662 square meters in Shirokanedai. It protects more than 200 plant species representative of the former Musashino landscape and hosts wildlife including raccoon dogs and mandarin ducks. It holds status as a Natural Monument and National Historic Site.

records.name: Arisugawa-no-miya Memorial Park
records.description: A 67,131-square-meter park in Minami-Azabu established in 1934 on the grounds of a former Edo-period villa donated by Prince Takamatsu. The hilly, wooded park has cascading valleys, ponds, an equestrian statue of Prince Arisugawa Taruhito, and a children's playground.

records.name: Nezu Museum
records.description: An art museum established in 1940 holding more than 7,400 pre-modern Japanese and East Asian artworks, including seven National Treasures. Its Kengo Kuma-designed building reopened in 2009 and is noted for its surrounding garden. The 'Irises' folding screen by Ogata Korin is displayed annually each spring.

records.name: Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum
records.description: The former home and studio of artist Taro Okamoto in Minami-Aoyama, where he lived and worked for 42 years until his death in 1996. The museum preserves his workshop as he kept it and displays his sculptures and paintings.

tips.text: Closed Tuesdays (except national holidays) and Dec 28-Jan 4; last admission is 30 minutes before closing.

records.name: Aqua Park Shinagawa
records.description: An urban aquarium on the grounds of the Shinagawa Prince Hotel in the Takanawa area, attracting more than 1.5 million visitors annually. It combines aquarium exhibits with dolphin shows and illuminated displays.

records.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum
records.description: An art museum in a 1933 Art Deco residence built for Prince Asaka Yasuhiko, with interiors by Henri Rapin and decorative glasswork by Rene Lalique. After serving as a prime ministerial residence and state guest house, it opened as a museum in 1983 and gained a Hiroshi Sugimoto-designed annex in 2014. The name 'Teien' refers to its surrounding Japanese garden.

records.name: Happo-en Garden
records.description: A Japanese garden in Shirokanedai with roots dating back over 400 years to the Edo period. The landscaped grounds, now also used as a wedding and event venue, are adjacent to Shirokanedai Station.
records.station: Shirokanedai Station (Namboku and Mita Lines, adjacent)

records.name: Akasaka Palace (State Guest House)
records.description: Japan's primary state guest house, built between 1899-1909 as a residence for the Crown Prince in a Neo-Baroque Western style. Following renovations completed in 1974, it has hosted state visits and international conferences, and was designated a National Treasure in 2009.

records.name: Nogi Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine established in 1923 honoring General Nogi Maresuke, a Sino-Japanese War military leader, and his wife Nogi Shizuko, who both died in 1912. The original structure was destroyed in 1945 air raids; the current building dates to 1962.
records.station: Nogizaka Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, exit 1, 1-minute walk)

records.name: Ark Hills
records.description: A 5.6-hectare mixed-use development in Akasaka that opened in 1986 as Japan's first large-scale private urban redevelopment complex. It combines office towers, residences, and a hotel, and is home to the Suntory Hall concert venue.
records.station: Kamiyacho Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line); Tameike-sanno Station (Ginza Line); Roppongi-itchome Station (Namboku Line)

records.name: Suntory Hall
records.description: A concert venue in the Ark Hills complex that opened in October 1986. Its 2,006-seat main hall uses a vineyard-style layout praised for its acoustics, and a smaller chamber hall seats up to 432. The main hall houses a custom pipe organ with 5,898 pipes.

records.name: Aoyama Cemetery
records.description: A 26.36-hectare public cemetery established in 1874 as Japan's first public burial ground, managed by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. It draws visitors during cherry blossom season and includes both a Japanese section with notable historical figures and a foreign section for international experts who aided Japan's modernization.

records.name: Kamezuka Park
records.description: A small neighborhood park of about 2.27 acres in Mita, established in 1952 on the Tsuki no Misaki plateau. Its name translates to 'turtle tomb park,' and the Saikai-ji temple sits adjacent to the grounds.

records.name: Zenpuku-ji Temple
records.description: A Jodo Shinshu temple in Azabu said to have been founded in 824 by Kukai as a Shingon temple, later brought into the Jodo Shinshu sect by Shinran. It is considered one of Tokyo's oldest temples after Sensoji, and under the 1859 Treaty of Amity and Commerce it housed the first United States legation in Tokyo.

records.name: Kyu-Shiba-rikyu Garden
records.description: A Japanese garden next to Hamamatsucho Station featuring a large ornamental pond fed by the tidal Sumida River. It is a former Edo-period daimyo garden now maintained by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government.

tips.text: Adult admission is 150 yen; last admission is 30 minutes before closing.

records.name: Minato City Local History Museum
records.description: A museum in a restored 1938 building, opened in 2018 as a base for learning about Minato City's nature, history, and culture through permanent and digital exhibits.

tips.text: Closed on New Year's holidays and the third Thursday of each month; the cafe and shop are free to enter without museum admission.

records.hours: 09:00–17:00 Mon-Fri, Sun, holidays; 09:00–20:00 Saturday (last entry 30 min before close)
records.station: Shirokanedai Station (Tokyo Metro Namboku Line / Toei Mita Line, exit 2, 21-minute walk)

records.name: Toranomon Hills Mori Tower
records.description: A 52-story skyscraper in Toranomon completed in May 2014 as part of the Toranomon Hills development, with office floors from the 6th to 35th floor. It is part of the wider Toranomon Hills complex that has since expanded with the Station Tower.
records.station: Toranomon Hills Station (1-minute walk); Toranomon Station (5-minute walk); Kamiyacho Station (6-minute walk)

records.name: Toranomon Kotohira Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine that is a branch of Kagawa Prefecture's Kotohira-gu (Konpira-san), first established on the Marugame domain's Edo residence in 1660 and moved to its current Toranomon site in 1679. It enshrines Emperor Sutoku and the deity Omononushi.

records.name: Toyokawa Inari Tokyo Betsuin
records.description: A Soto Zen Buddhist temple branch in Akasaka dedicated to the Inari deity, popularly known for its rows of fox statues. It functions both as a temple and as a spot for prayers related to business and prosperity.
records.station: Akasaka-mitsuke Station (exit B, 5-minute walk); Nagatacho Station (exit 7, 5-minute walk)

records.name: TEPIA Advanced Technology Gallery
records.description: A free educational gallery in Kita-Aoyama showcasing cutting-edge technology aimed at young people, organized into themed zones on society, economy, and the environment.
records.hours: 09:30–17:00 Tuesday-Sunday and holidays (closed Mondays and New Year's)
records.station: Gaienmae Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, exit 2b, 4-minute walk)

records.name: MoN Takanawa (The Museum of Narratives)
records.description: A museum within the Takanawa Gateway City development that opened March 28, 2026, designed by Kengo Kuma & Associates. Its name references the historical Takanawa Great Wooden Gate and the modern Takanawa Gateway Station, and its displays combine traditional Japanese culture with future-facing themes.

records.name: Keio University Old Library and Enzetsukan (Mita Campus)
records.description: Two historic buildings on Keio University's Mita Campus: the Enzetsukan, built in 1875 as Japan's first public lecture hall and relocated to its current site in 1924, and the Gothic-style Old Library. Both are designated National Important Cultural Properties.
